types_of_current.Direct_Current_DC: Electricity that flows in only one direction. It cannot be stepped up or down easily for long distances.
types_of_current.Alternating_Current_AC: Electricity that flows in two directions (back and forth). This is the type used in the national grid because it can be changed in voltage using transformers.
types_of_current.visual_reference: [IMAGE_007: Graph showing DC vs AC flow lines]

ugandan_power_sources.Hydro_Electricity: Main source in Uganda. Generated by moving water in the Nile. Key dams: Nalubaale and Bujagali in Jinja.
ugandan_power_sources.Thermal_Electricity: Produced by burning fossil fuels (diesel, petrol, coal). Most expensive because fuel must be bought constantly.
ugandan_power_sources.Solar_Electricity: Energy trapped from the sun using solar cells/panels.
ugandan_power_sources.Geothermal: Heat from underground hot rocks near volcanoes used to create steam.
ugandan_power_sources.Nuclear: Produced by the splitting of Uranium atoms.

energy_conversions.Hydroelectric_Dam_Sequence: Potential Energy (stored water) -> Kinetic Energy (falling water) -> Mechanical Energy (spinning turbine) -> Electrical Energy (generator).
energy_conversions.visual_reference: [IMAGE_009: Flowchart of Energy in a Dam]

resource_classification.Renewable: Resources that do not run out (Sun, Water, Wind).
resource_classification.Non_Renewable: Resources that take millions of years to form and will run out (Fossil fuels like Coal and Oil).
